newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro/U.S. stocks slip from record highs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro/U.S. stocks slip from record highs.

text.p: Investors went on a buying spree on Tuesday, sending several European bourses to new highs and extending Wall Street's record-breaking performance, but markets later slipped back as they cashed in some profits.
The London stock market, Europe's busiest, still scored a record close but ended below its highs after the much bigger New York market failed to live up to its early promise.
Traders also reported caution ahead of key U.S. and British data later in the week -- particularly U.S. September consumer price (CPI) figures on Wednesday.
Frankfurt, Zurich, Amsterdam, Madrid, Stockholm, Oslo and Budapest were among bourses scaling new peaks during the day and the Paris bourse hit its highest level since May 1994.
Elsewhere, oil prices traded near six-year highs after an advance which has boosted them by 40 percent in four months.

On the foreign exchanges, the pound drew further strength and the dollar ended European trading near 33-month peaks against the yen and just below 18-week highs against the mark, boosted by the rally in share prices and dearer oil.

Market analysts forecast more gains for European shares if a "dream combination" of steady economic growth and low inflation lasts, with investors likely to pump more cash in as prospects for corporate earnings and dividend payouts improve.
"The economic background is about as good as it gets," said Peter Sullivan, European equity strategist at U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs in London.

On Monday, the Dow Jones industrial average ended above 6,000 for the first time, jumping 40.62 to 6,010. Healthy company earnings news helped it hit a new all-time high of 6,044.29 early on Tuesday before profit-taking set in and it then hit a low of 6,000.31, down nearly 10 points.
"I'm not at all surprised that we're seeing some profit-taking here," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany in New York.
The index of 30 U.S. blue-chip share prices has had a dizzying rise, soaring through 5,000 only last November, nine months after topping 4,000.

London's stock market had already breached the 4,000 mark on the FTSE 100 share index and made further progress on Tuesday, supported by higher bonds and an agreed bid for international exhibitions group Blenheim, before later disappointment with Wall Street.

"We had a record but the market started to look a bit tired...people are slowly learning the painful lesson that what goes on in the early hours of Wall Street is not particularly indicative of the full session performance," one trader said.
Germany's DAX index opened at a record high above 2,700 and added to its gains, boosted by Wall Street's strength, higher bonds and a strong dollar -- good news for German exporters.
French shares ended at a new closing high for the year but off their highest levels.

High oil prices weakened the yen, in view of Japan's dependence on imported oil, while helping to send the pound to 21-month highs against the mark, 11-month peaks versus the dollar and more than three-year highs against the yen.
The Japanese currency was also under pressure ahead of Sunday's election.

London November futures for international benchmark North Sea Brent blend crude were down 20 cents a barrel at $24.66 in late afternoon, having earlier hit a new post-Gulf War high of $25.06 to add 20 cents to an 88 cent jump on Monday.
But despite the short-term boost dearer oil has given to various markets, economists and analysts said soaring oil prices could reignite dormant inflationary pressures.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT

The dollar was quoted around 1.5395 marks and 112.30 yen in late European business, compared with 1.5293 and 111.60 a day earlier. The pound gained to $1.5830 and 2.4380 marks from $1.5805 and 2.4174.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 12.1 points higher at 4,050.8, compared with an earlier peak of 4,063.2.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt ended bourse floor trade up 34.57 at a record close of 2,728.45, near its intra-day peak of 2,728.64. It finished later electronic trade at 2,718.73.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 24.66 at 2,168.28 but below a high of 2,176.45 hit earlier.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold ended London trading at $381.45 an ounce after being fixed at $381 in the afternoon, unchanged from the morning fix but below Monday's London close of $381.65. Silver ended two cents lower at $5.04.
